title: Pasiva de opinión: it is said that…, he is believed to…

rule.title: Passive reporting structures
rule.explanation:
En noticias y textos formales contamos lo que dice la gente sin decir quién. Hay dos estructuras:
- «It is said» / «believed» / «thought» / «expected» / «reported that» + frase: «It is said that the album is the surprise of the year.»
- Sujeto + «is said» / «believed» / «thought» / «expected» + «to» + verbo: «The album is said to be the surprise of the year.»

Si lo que se dice se refiere al pasado, «to have» + participio:
- «The band is believed to have signed a deal.»
- «Sam is thought to have written most of the songs.»

Si se refiere a algo que está pasando, «to be» + «-ing»:
- «They are reported to be recording a new album.»

«Be supposed to» significa «se supone que» (lo que se espera o lo que dicen):
- «He's supposed to be in London this week.»
- «You're supposed to check in two hours before.»

Ojo: con la estructura de sujeto, el verbo de la frase va en infinitivo: «He is said to be rich» (nunca «He is said that he is rich»).

rows: It is said that he is rich.
He is said to be rich.
He is said to have left.
They are said to be recording.
